hook.line: Don Hernando doesn't do maybes. Simón is missing, the rains are coming, and he makes a promise in front of the whole café.
hook.es: Te prometo que lo encontraré antes de las lluvias.
hook.en: I promise you I'll find him before the rains.

examples.en: I'll call you tomorrow. (to a friend)
It will rain in Bogotá tomorrow.
Will you help me? (to a friend)

examples.es: El café abrirá a las siete.
examples.en: The café will open at seven.
I'll tell you tomorrow. (to a friend)

rule:
You already know these forms from guessing. Now they do their other job: the real future, said like you mean it.

*llamaré*: I'll call
*llamarás*: you'll call
*llamará*: he, she or you (*usted*) will call
*llamaremos*: we'll call
*llamarán*: they or you all will call

Same short stems as before: *tendré*, *sabré*, *haré*, *podré*, *vendré*, plus *diré* (*decir*), *saldré* (*salir*), *pondré* (*poner*), *querré* (*querer*).

The catch for English speakers: for everyday plans, Colombians still say *voy a*: *Mañana voy a trabajar.* This future is for promises (*Te llamaré*), forecasts (*Mañana lloverá*), the news and formal plans (*El café abrirá a las siete*), and big statements (*No será fácil*). It sounds a little more serious, and that's the point.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the simple future (*futuro simple*). Its guessing use is called the future of probability.

options: It will rain in the afternoon.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *llamaré* or *llamará* and type the whole sentence: *Te ___ mañana.* (I'll call you tomorrow.)
yourTurn.why: I will is *-é*: *llamaré*. *Llamará* is he or she.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *hará* or *hacerá* and type the whole sentence: *Don Hernando lo ___.* (Don Hernando will do it.)
yourTurn.why: *Hacer* is one of the short ones: *hará*.

yourTurn.prompt: Promise a friend: I'll help you.
yourTurn.why: A promise is the classic home of *-ré*.

yourTurn.prompt: Read out the forecast: It will rain in Bogotá tomorrow.

yourTurn.why: *No* goes before the verb, and *ser* keeps its whole infinitive: *será*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Diré algo.* (I won't say anything.)
yourTurn.why: *No* before the verb, and *algo* turns into *nada*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the casual line into a promise: *Mañana te escribo.* (I'll write to you tomorrow.)
yourTurn.why: *Escribir* plus *-é* gives *escribiré*, and it sounds like you mean it.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Tener* shortens to *tendr-* before the ending, just as when you were guessing.
The accent is part of the ending: *-ré*, stressed at the very end.
*Hacer* is one of the short ones: *hará*.
After *voy a* the verb stays in its dictionary form. It's one future or the other, never both.

personal: Make one promise to someone in your life, in Spanish. Start with *Te prometo que* and finish with a *-ré* verb.
